chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about nosebleeding, cupping, and every flowing blood, and he said: There is no wudu (ablution) in this. Wudu (ablution) is only from your two ends with which Allah has blessed you.

key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ: your two ends; the two bodily outlets referred to in rulings of wudu

ai.seo_question: Does nosebleeding or cupping invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that bleeding such as nosebleeding and cupping does not invalidate wudu (ablution). It restricts the causes of wudu (ablution) to what exits from the two bodily passages, clarifying a matter of ritual purity in fiqh.
